chunks: And from him (al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Saffar) from al-Barqi from Sa'd from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who is in his house and he is praying, and he thinks that the night prayer (Isha) is upon him. Then another person enters through the door and says, 'It is morning.' Should he repeat the Witr prayer or not, or should he repeat something from his prayer? He said: 'He repeats if he prayed as one who is morning (i.e., after Fajr time entered).'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: It is only appropriate for him to repeat it if he prayed as one who is morning, because when he becomes morning, the time for the obligatory prayer has narrowed, so it is not permissible for him to pray a voluntary prayer. Therefore, if he prayed it, he must repeat it because he prayed it outside its time.

key_terms.مُصْبِحاً: As one who is morning (praying after Fajr time has entered)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on repeating Witr or night prayer if morning enters while one is still praying?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the ruling for Witr and optional night prayers when dawn breaks during or immediately after the prayer, establishing that they must be repeated if performed after the Fajr time has entered. Shaykh al-Tusi adds scholarly context by explaining that once the obligatory Fajr time begins, one cannot validly offer supererogatory prayers, as the time for the obligatory duty has superseded the window for voluntary acts.
